title: Optically Addressable Spins in a Metal–Organic Framework
abstract: Abstract Molecular spins supporting optically detected magnetic resonance (ODMR) offer unique opportunities for quantum sensing and many-body physics by combining the sensitivity and spatial resolution offered by optical spin detection with the capacity for bottom-up assembly and chemical control. Metal–organic frameworks (MOFs) are a promising architecture to leverage such opportunities since they offer control over spin placement, tunable porosity and large internal surface areas for efficient integration with sensing targets, and a richly tunable chemical space. However, optical spin readout has not been demonstrated in a MOF. Here, we report the first successful optical detection of spins in a MOF. We use a porphyrin-based aluminum MOF (Al-PMOF), which supports efficient triplet generation on the porphyrin chromophore ligands. Using electron paramagnetic resonance, we demonstrate that these triplet states support a spin coherence time (T2) on the order of a few microseconds at 50 K. Importantly, we successfully detect optically detected magnetic resonance of these triplets using near-infrared ODMR at 77 K. Optical spin readout in a MOF paves the way for next-generation quantum sensing applications that leverage bottom-up assembly.

title: Mortise‐and‐Tenon Molecular Joint Covalent Organic Frameworks With Tunable Topology for Photothermal‐Catalytic Cross‐Dehydrogenative Coupling
abstract: ABSTRACT The controllable regulation of dimensionality and interpenetration in covalent organic frameworks (COFs) is crucial for optimizing photocatalytic performance, yet the translation of 3D COFs from structural construction to functional customization remains challenging. Here, we successfully designed a series of mortise‐and‐tenon molecular joint COFs by rationally engineering a twisted tetraphthaldehyde ligand bearing π‐conjugated “clips”. Stepwise extension of the “clips” enables topological evolution from 2D to twofold interpenetrated 3D, and ultimately to noninterpenetrated 3D structure. Notably, DHP‐CuPor‐COF with noninterpenetrated 3D structure amplifies light‐harvesting efficiency and substrate accessibility, enabling superior photothermal conversion and catalytic performance over its 2D and twofold interpenetrated 3D counterparts. To the best of our knowledge, it delivers highly efficient photothermal‐catalytic C─X (X = O, S) bond formation for selective transformation of phenolic compounds via cross‐dehydrogenative coupling (CDC) reactions (conv., >90% and yield, >80%), markedly outperforming conventional thermal catalysis. The high efficiency arises from the synergistic of open 3D channels, abundant Cu‐porphyrin active sites and strong photothermal effect. This work provides an innovative strategy to tune the topological chemistry of COFs for advanced photocatalytic applications.

title: Highly Sensitive Broadband Photodetectors Based on Donor–Acceptor 2D Conjugated Coordination Polymers
abstract: ABSTRACT Two‐dimensional (2D) semiconductors are highly desirable for broadband photodetection but are often constrained by their limited optical absorption and inefficient exciton dissociation. In this study, we report a donor–acceptor‐engineered 2D conjugated coordination polymer (c‐CP), Ni‐TABQ (TABQ = tetraaminobenzoquinone), as a narrow‐bandgap semiconductor. The TABQ ligands integrate electron‐rich amino donors and electron‐deficient quinone carbonyl acceptors within the same molecular backbone, endowing the Ni‐TABQ lattice with strong intramolecular charge‐transfer absorption and a built‐in driving force for charge separation. Benefiting from strong broadband absorption and high charge‐carrier mobility, the vapor‐phase‐grown Ni‐TABQ thin films enable photodetection from 350 to 1400 nm under a 3 V bias, with a measurable response tail above 1150 nm, further achieving a responsivity of up to 3.1 A W −1 , a specific detectivity of up to 6.58 × 10 10 Jones (625 nm at ∼85 µW cm −2 ), and a response time of ∼206 µs, while maintaining stable operation at 3 V over 8500 s of continuous cycling. These metrics compare favorably with state‐of‐the‐art broadband photodetectors based on standalone 2D materials, establishing donor–acceptor molecular engineering within the 2D metal‐organic lattice as an effective strategy for advancing high‐performance 2D optoelectronic devices.

title: Enhanced Electrochemical C–N Coupling for Glycine Synthesis via an Active Hydrogen Pump
abstract: ABSTRACT Direct electrochemical C–N coupling of abundant carbon and nitrogen feedstocks offers a sustainable route to glycine synthesis, yet achieving high efficiency remains challenging. Here, we develop an In–Bi catalyst by incorporating oxophilic indium (In) into a bismuth (Bi) matrix. During the co‐reduction of oxalic acid and NO 3 − , the In–Bi catalyst delivers an exceptional Faradaic efficiency toward glycine (FE Glycine ) of 83.3% with an industrial‐level current density of 361.3 mA cm −2 , together with a glycine production rate of 4.3 mol h −1 g cat. −1 . It outperforms pristine Bi and previously reported state‐of‐the‐art catalysts. Large‐scale glycine electrosynthesis is further demonstrated over a 10 cm 2 In–Bi electrode, achieving a total current of 1.5 A with FE Glycine of 68.5% and yielding 1.4 g of glycine in 6 h. Mechanistically, oxalic acid and NO 3 − first form glyoxylic acid oxime (GAO). Subsequently, In sites act as an “active hydrogen pump” to accelerate H 2 O dissociation, providing abundant surface‐active hydrogen (*H) for efficient GAO hydrogenation to glycine. Meanwhile, the incorporation of In modulates the electronic structure of the Bi matrix, enhancing GAO adsorption and electron transfer. The synergistic regulation of *H supply and electronic structure accelerates the conversion of GAO to glycine, resulting in superior performance of In–Bi.

title: A Hydrogen-Bonded Metal–Organic Framework for CO2 Capture and Natural Gas Upgrading
abstract: Abstract Efficient separation of CO2/N2 (flue gas), CO2/CH4 (natural gas), and light hydrocarbons is important in industry but remains a critical challenge. The development of versatile adsorbents capable of addressing multiple industrially relevant gas separations is therefore highly desirable. Herein, we report the synthesis of a three-dimensional (3D) hydrogen-bonded organic framework (HOF), designated ZNU-69, constructed through the interlayer hydrogen-bonding self-assembly of two-dimensional (2D) metal–organic framework (MOF) layers. Single-component adsorption isotherms reveal that ZNU-69 exhibits preferential uptake of CO2, C2H6, and C3H8 over CH4 and N2. IAST selectivity calculations at 298 K and 1 bar yield values as high as 473 for CO2/N2 (15/85), 127 for CO2/CH4 (50/50), 596 for C3H8/CH4 (50/50), and 54 for C2H6/CH4 (50/50). Theoretical calculations elucidate the microscopic adsorption mechanism, revealing that the strong binding energies, along with multiple hydrogen-bonding and van der Waals interactions with the framework, are responsible for the observed affinity and selectivity. Dynamic breakthrough experiments and cyclic tests further confirm its excellent separation performance and robust regeneration stability. This work provides a strategy for designing multifunctional MOF/HOF hybrid adsorbents that synergistically combine high selectivity with broad applicability.

title: Heterogeneous Electric Double Layer with Ion‐Transport Pathways for Practical Zinc‐Ion Batteries
abstract: ABSTRACT Manipulating the electric double layer (EDL) structure at nanoscale remains largely underexplored yet extremely challenging for practical Ah‐level aqueous zinc‐ion batteries (AZIBs). Here, we construct a heterogeneous nanostructured EDL with intrinsic ion‐transport pathways via cation‐anion coordination strategy, which synergistically enhances the thermodynamic stability and kinetic reversibility of the Zn anode. In‐situ characterizations and theoretical simulations demonstrate that the long‐chain ionic additive triggers the interfacial ion rearrangement and assembly within the EDL, where hydrophobic carbon chains self‐aggregate into dense apolar nanodomains, and cationic groups electrostatically attract anions and co‐assemble to form interconnected polar nanodomains. This uniquely heterogeneous EDL thermodynamically confines H 2 O activity and efficiently inhibits side reactions. Meanwhile, the interconnected polar ion‐transport pathways accelerate Zn 2+ migration and desolvation kinetics, achieving an ultrahigh Zn 2+ transference number (0.89) and dendrite‐free Zn deposition. Consequently, Zn//Zn cell delivers stable cycling over 1,200 h (25 mA cm −2 , 12.5 mAh cm −2 ) and Zn//NVO full cell retains 100% capacity after 30,000 cycles at 5 A g −1 . Furthermore, 0.2‐Ah and 1.1‐Ah pouch cells exhibit stable operation for 2,500 and 257 cycles, respectively. This work establishes a new paradigm for EDL nanostructure engineering, advancing practical AZIBs.

title: Engineering a multifunctional bioactive coordination polymer nanoplatform for inflammation-responsive bone regeneration
abstract: Inflammatory bone diseases are closely associated with impaired osteogenic differentiation of mesenchymal stem cells (MSCs) and excessive inflammatory signaling. Sinomenine (SIN) exhibits anti-inflammatory activity; however, its therapeutic application is limited by poor bioavailability. In this work, a multifunctional nanoplatform (CS-1@CP1@SIN) was constructed for SIN delivery and electrochemical sensing applications. The nanocomposite exhibited a mesoporous structure, structural stability, and improved electrochemical response characteristics. In a TNF-α-induced inflammatory MSC model, CS-1@CP1@SIN improved cell viability, reduced the expression of pro-inflammatory cytokines (IL-1β and IL-6), and enhanced the expression of osteogenic markers (Runx2, ALP, and OCN). In addition, the CS-1@CP1@SIN-modified electrode exhibited enhanced electrocatalytic activity toward tert-butylhydroquinone (TBHQ), enabling sensitive and reliable electrochemical detection. These results demonstrate that the proposed nanoplatform integrates anti-inflammatory therapy and electrochemical sensing functions, providing a multifunctional strategy for inflammatory bone disease treatment and food antioxidant monitoring.

title: Metal-organic frameworks for separation of organic compounds in liquid phase
abstract: Abstract Liquid-phase separation underpins numerous sectors of modern chemical industry, yet achieving high selectivity for separation of mixtures of organic compounds remains a persistent challenge. Metal-organic frameworks (MOFs), showing exceptional tunability in composition, topology and pore environment, hold unique promise to address this challenge. This review surveys recent progress in studies of MOFs for the selective extraction and purification of organic substrates in liquid phase, with a focus on elucidating the mechanism of selectivity. Function-directed design principles, encompassing tailored bonding interactions, programmable supramolecular environments and pore-confinement effects, are discussed as enabling precise control over transport processes. These concepts are examined across key application domains, including removal of pollutants in water treatment, the separation of structurally similar hydrocarbons in petrochemical refinery and the selective discrimination of daily pharmaceuticals. Opportunities for the next generation of MOF-based sorbents are outlined, highlighting challenges associated with scalability and long-term operational stability, and the growing roles of artificial intelligence (AI)-guided discovery in developing sustainable separation technologies are further projected.

title: Freezing-induced solid-liquid microphase separation for self-assembly of functional nucleic acid nanoparticles
abstract: In nature, nuclear DNA complexed with histone form highly condensed chromatin via loop extrusion and microphase separation, yielding physically constrained solid-like structures. Inspired by this natural compaction, here we demonstrate that freezing-induced crystallization pressure and freeze-concentration effects trigger solid-liquid microphase separation for efficient DNA compression. Freezing compress various nucleic acids (single stranded DNA, molecular beacons, siRNA, plasmid DNA) into high-density states that self-assemble into nanoparticles (DNA-NPs, MB-NPs, siBcl-2-NPs, siPLK1-NPs, pEGFP-NPs). Molecular dynamics simulations reveal that ice crystal growth increases solute concentration, enhancing DNA intermolecular interactions to form supramolecular chains. Stress at advancing ice-liquid interfaces further orders and compacts these supramolecular chains into nanoparticles. In breast cancer cells, MB-NPs detect miRNA-21; siBcl-2-NPs downregulate Bcl-2 protein; siPLK1-NPs exhibited antitumor effects; and pEGFP-NPs mediate green fluorescent protein (GFP) expression. This freeze-induced self-assembly strategy replaces chemical synthesis with physical constraints, establishing a versatile platform for facile production of nucleic acid nanoparticles. Efficent delivery of various nucleic acids in vitro and in vivo remains challenging. Here, the authors use freezing-induced condensation and microphase separation to compress nucleic acids into functional nanoparticles, without excipients, validated the bioactivity in vitro and in vivo.

title: Nanocavity Confining Platinum Nanoclusters Enhances Photocatalytic Two‐Electron Oxygen Reduction for Wound Healing
abstract: ABSTRACT Photocatalytic two‐electron oxygen reduction reaction (ORR) toward H 2 O 2 synthesis is a compelling approach for clinical antibacterial applications. Yet its selectivity is hampered by the competing four‐electron ORR, which compromises both H 2 O 2 generation kinetics and antibacterial efficiency. Herein, we report a new nanoscale confinement strategy for the controllable synthesis of covalent organic frameworks (COFs) confining isolated platinum nanoclusters (NCs) to enhance Pauling‐type of O 2 adsorption to achieve two‐electron oxygen reduction for efficient antibacterial therapy. The resulting Tfp‐Db COFs@Pt NCs exhibits a significantly higher H 2 O 2 formation kinetics (3.12 × 10− 3 mol L −1 h −1 ) than Tfp‐Db COFs@Pt nanoparticles (1.55 × 10 −3 mol L −1 h −1 ), with 2e − ORR selectivity increased from 45.0% to 86.0%. Experimental and theoretical results reveal a two‐step single electron oxygen reduction pathway for H 2 O 2 photosynthesis over Tfp‐Db COFs@Pt NCs. The Tfp‐Db COFs@Pt NCs exhibits excellent sterilization efficiencies of 5.0 log 10 CFU mL −1 and 5.2 log 10 CFU mL −1 against S. aureus and E. coli , respectively, exceeding most reported materials. Furthermore, Tfp‐Db COFs@Pt NCs facilitate the regeneration of infectious wounds, with the efficiency of nearly 100% on day 10, outperforming previously reported bionanomaterials. Collectively, this work presents a new strategy for regulating the Pauling‐type of O 2 adsorption to enhance the photocatalytic H 2 O 2 formation for wound healing application.

title: Charge Storage and Dark Photocatalysis in Multivariate Ti‐Based Metal‐Organic Frameworks
abstract: ABSTRACT “Dark photocatalysis” decouples electron storage from photoconversion, offering a promising route to buffer solar intermittency, however requiring precise control of light‐matter interactions. Metal–organic frameworks (MOFs) provide a platform to tailor these interactions at the molecular level through judicious selection of organic linkers and interconnected metal nodes. This study advances design principles for dark photocatalysis by integrating two linkers with complementary light‐interaction roles in a multivariate (MTV) COK‐47 series. Varying the ratio between biphenyl dicarboxylate ( biph ) and bipyridine dicarboxylate ( bipy ) linker shows that under continuous irradiation (365 nm), COK‐47 biph is the most photocatalytically active member, surpassing COK‐47 bipy by threefold. In contrast, COK‐47 bipy exhibits an eightfold increase in photocharging capacity, revealed by a multispectroscopic approach, evidencing the formation of Ti 3+ and reduced linker species as storage unit. The stored charges drive methyl viologen (MV) reduction and H 2 evolution in the dark. Notably, the mixed‐linker material COK‐47 50‐50 combines both advantages, delivering near‐maximal H 2 production under illumination while retaining substantial charge storage capability, achieving the highest MV reduction activity and second‐highest dark H 2 evolution in the series. These findings connect framework composition to light‐matter interaction, charge storage capacity, catalytic activity, and establish a design strategy for multifunctional dark photocatalytic materials.

title: Regulated Co‐Solvation in Gel Polymer Electrolyte Enables Rapid and Selective Li + Ion Transport for High‐Rate Lithium Metal Batteries
abstract: ABSTRACT The development of gel polymer electrolytes (GPEs) suitable for high‐rate lithium metal batteries (LMBs) is urgently needed but remains inherently challenging. This difficulty originates from the competition between the polymer network and the liquid electrolyte for lithium ion (Li + ) coordination. Polymer‐dominated coordination traps Li + and slows transport, while solvent‐dominated solvation permits uncontrolled anion migration and causes concentration polarization. Here, we resolve this challenge by establishing a matched polymer–electrolyte co‐solvation state, which enables rapid and selective Li + transport via a cooperative mechanism. We implement this concept through a dual‐regulated weak‐coordination gel polymer electrolyte (DWGPE), which comprises a fluorinated polymer backbone that attenuates Li + binding, an amide‐functionalized crosslinker that immobilizes anions via hydrogen bonding, and a weakly solvating adiponitrile‐based liquid phase. Molecular dynamics simulations reveal a cooperative transport mechanism that integrates polymer‐assisted hopping and solvent‐mediated vehicular diffusion, while suppressing anion mobility. Consequently, Li||DWGPE||LFP coin cells sustain 10 000 cycles at 6 C with 65% capacity retention, corresponding to an ultralow capacity decay of 0.003% per cycle. Our DWGPE also operates stably with high‐voltage NCM811 cathodes and in ampere‐hour‐level pouch cells. This work establishes polymer–electrolyte co‐solvation as a design framework for high‐performance GPEs toward fast‐charging LMBs.

title: Self-Catalyzed Hastelloy Fiber Paper (HAP) Porous Transport Layer for Oxygen Evolution Reaction in Anion Exchange Membrane Water Electrolysis
abstract: Abstract Hastelloy fiber paper (HAP) can be used as the oxygen evolution reaction porous transport layer (PTL) without using a catalyst layer in anion exchange membrane water electrolysis. It is combined with Ru on nickel fiber paper (NFP) (hydrogen evolution reaction PTL) to form an asymmetric Ru/NFP(−)//HAP(+) single-cell system. The experimental results for electrodeposited Co(OH)2 on HAP are also demonstrated for comparison. At 70 °C, the cell delivers 725.67 mA cm–2 at 1.8 V under cathode-wet conditions and maintains 701.34 mA cm–2 under cathode-dry operation. A 5000-cycle accelerated stress test (AST) confirms the good operational stability of the system under dynamic cycling conditions. In addition, the effect of Co(OH)2 electrodeposition on the HAP anode was further investigated to show the current density decreases to 485.59 mA cm–2 at 1.8 V when operated at 70 °C. The AST stability also degrades with Co(OH)2 deposition. Further analysis indicates that the electrodeposited Co(OH)2 coating may alter the pore structure and surface wettability of the catalyst layer, leading to mass-transport limitations at high current densities, including hindered ion transport and inefficient oxygen bubble removal.

title: Charge Transfer Mediators in Photoelectrochemical Water Splitting: From Interfacial Regulation to Rational Design
abstract: ABSTRACT Photoelectrochemical (PEC) water splitting is a promising route for solar‐to‐chemical energy conversion and storage, yet its efficiency remains limited by interfacial charge recombination, inefficient carrier extraction, and sluggish reaction kinetics. Charge transfer mediators have emerged as critical interfacial components bridging photoelectrodes, cocatalysts, and conductive substrates, enabling directional carrier transport, suppressed recombination, and enhanced catalytic activity. However, their roles, design principles, and mechanisms in PEC systems remain insufficiently understood. This review systematically defines charge transfer mediators in PEC water splitting, clarifies their multifunctional roles in charge transfer, charge storage, and interfacial protection, and summarizes representative material platforms, including carbon‐based materials, MXenes, metal oxides, molecular materials, nonmetal nitrides, and other emerging mediators. Particular emphasis is placed on the relationship between mediator structures, interfacial configurations, electronic properties, and PEC performance. Advanced characterization techniques and theoretical approaches for elucidating charge transfer pathways and reaction mechanisms are also discussed to establish structure‐property‐performance correlations. Finally, key challenges and future perspectives are highlighted, positioning charge transfer mediators as an emerging paradigm for constructing efficient, stable, and practical PEC systems.

title: A high-performance synthetic micro-mesoporous activated carbon obtained from virgin and recycled PVDC with exceptional biobutanol separation performance
abstract: The effective recovery of biobutanol from fermentation vapor streams hinges on the development of highly selective adsorbents that can efficiently capture butanol in the presence of excess water. This paper addresses this challenge through the synthesis and characterization of tailored activated carbons. Using a high-purity polyvinylidene chloride (PVDC) precursor, in both virgin and recycled forms, a series of carbons were prepared by varying the duration of physical CO2 activation process (up to 26 h). The study establishes a clear link between these synthesis conditions and the resulting porous structure. All synthesized activated carbons displayed Type V water adsorption isotherms proving a high degree of hydrophobicity which further enhanced with increased activation time and burn-off. The nature of butanol adsorption was strongly linked to the pore structure; materials with shorter activation times and lower burn-off exhibited Type I isotherms indicative of micropore filling, while those with longer activation times and wider pores showed Type V isotherms, reflecting a cooperative adsorption mechanism. The derived activated carbons demonstrated a very high adsorption capacity for butanol vapor (0.9 g/g at 200 Pa and 40°C), significantly higher than values reported in literature for other adsorbents. Dynamic breakthrough experiments using a mixed butanol-water vapor stream validated the enhanced separation performance with a dynamic capacity very close to the equilibrium capacity. The material obtained from recycled PVDC showed excellent adsorption properties, superior to commercial benchmark materials, opening perspectives for the valorization of waste PVDC into a renewable, high grade functional porous solid.

title: Planar Macromolecular Semiconductors Enable Fast Electron‐Ion Transport Kinetics for High‐Performance Zinc‐Organic Batteries
abstract: ABSTRACT Polymer cathodes featuring versatile designable redox‐active motifs and structural anti‐dissolution in aqueous electrolytes have attracted interest for advancing zinc‐organic batteries. However, their implementation is hindered by insulating electronic properties and sluggish ion transport, both arising from twisted molecule chains with poor structural planarity, which limits active‐site accessibility and capacity delivery. Here we design planar macromolecular semiconductors (PMSs) by fusing a four‐electron pyrene‐4,5,9,10‐tetraone acceptor and a two‐electron tetraminobenzoquinone donator into long‐range conjugated polymeric skeletons through intermolecular π – π interactions. The highly π ‐extended planarity endows PMSs with a semiconducting property (7.64 × 10 −7 S cm −1 ) that promotes efficient electron delocalization, and yields the highest ion diffusion coefficient (6.52 × 10 −7 cm 2 s −1 ) among reported organic cathodes. Leveraging synergistic fast electron‐ion transport kinetics, the long‐range stacking of molecular planes minimizes conformational disorder, enabling near‐complete utilization (98.4%) of redox‐active quinone−phenazine motifs with an ultralow activation energy (0.19 eV). Consequently, Zn||PMSs battery liberates high capacities (442/263 mAh g −1 at 0.2/100 A g −1 ), alongside a long lifespan (60,000 cycles). Besides, PMSs cathode enables a 348 mAh zinc pouch cell with a high mass loading (20 mg cm −2 ) to operate stably for 1000 cycles. This work provides a promising direction to design planar organic semiconductors for boosting electron‐ion migration kinetics toward better zinc batteries.

title: A soluble conductive chromium coordination polymer with radical ligands and non-integer redox states
abstract: There are few conductive metal-organic materials that are solution processible or that feature electron-accepting conductive units. Thus, a soluble, semiconductive coordination polymer (1n+)x (n = 1 – 3) was developed by linking CrIII ions with electron-deficient back-to-back bis-terpyridine (btpy) ligands. CrIII promotes reduction of these ligands under mild conditions (starting at −0.16 V vs. Fc+/0), providing the first extended material with btpy•− or btpy2− units. Interestingly, (1n+)x undergoes non-integer redox changes (∣Δn∣ < 1) in DMF solution, representing emergent electronic behavior that leads to a moderately high solid-state conductivity of 3.9 x 10−3 S cm−1 when n = 1.5. These solution-phase/solid-state correlations present a promising way to examine and tune the electronic properties of metal-organic radical materials.

title: Self-buoyant cell-spheroid culture programming multi-spheroid assembly
abstract: Tempo-spatially controlled culture and assembly of cellular spheroids are fundamental in engineering tissue-like assembloids for scalable application, yet remain a technical challenge. Here, we show self-buoyant culture of cell spheroids and programmable assembly of multi-spheroid by microbubbles in a high-throughput, external field-free and miniaturized format. This approach allows one-step engineering of biocompatible cell-adhesive buoyancy interface that lifts the self-adaptive levitation growth of reliable one-drop-one-spheroid in an array without requiring any external fields. Using this self-floating spheroidal microarray, we find that a facile droplet ‘kiss’ facilitates the buoyancy-driven ultrafast transfer (∼1 s) of spheroids between top-down adjacent droplets, thus achieving rapid spheroid relocation, media exchange, and drug administration in parallel. Such a self-buoyant approach allows programmable horizontal/vertical bioassembly and enhanced fusion of homo/heterogeneous multi-spheroids into different “buoyantoid” patterns via sequential flash transfer along droplet array. This self-powered design provides a promising tool to enable mass production and smart manipulation of encoded assembloids for precision medicine, tissue engineering and high-throughput drug screening.

title: One‐Pot Construction of Amine‐Linked Covalent Organic Frameworks via Photoredox‐Catalyzed Reductive Amination
abstract: ABSTRACT Photocatalytic synthesis, as a green and efficient approach to organic synthesis, has been widely adopted in various organic transformations; however, its application in the synthesis of covalent organic frameworks (COFs) remains in the early stages of development. Moreover, to date, no photocatalytic approach has been employed for the synthesis of amine‐linked COFs, which feature a higher density of basic sites and demonstrate enhanced stability. Herein, we report a novel one‐pot photoredox‐catalyzed reductive amination strategy for the synthesis of amine‐linked COFs under ambient conditions for the first time. Based on this strategy, a series of amine‐linked COFs were synthesized. Among these materials, DT‐Am‐COF exhibits excellent photocatalytic activity and demonstrates high efficiency as a catalyst for the light‐driven oxidative hydrogenation of arylboronic acids and oxidation of sulfides. This study not only presents an effective method for the synthesis of amine‐linked COFs, but also opens new insights into their preparation.

title: Interfacial Confinement Enables Dual Hosting of Sulfur Mustard and Mustard Sulfoxide in NU-1000
abstract: Abstract Zirconium-based metal–organic frameworks have emerged as promising materials for the capture and detoxification of chemical warfare agents, but the molecular mechanism by which a hierarchical MOF differentiates a hydrophobic reactant from its oxidized product remains incompletely understood. Here, we use molecular dynamics simulations, grand-canonical Monte Carlo adsorption calculations, and periodic density functional theory to examine the dual-hosting behavior of NU-1000 toward sulfur mustard (HD) and mustard sulfoxide (HDO). Rather than treating NU-1000 only as an adsorbent or oxidation catalyst, we resolve how its internal micropore, mesopore, and c-pore interfaces impose distinct confinement environments on reactant and product species. Density functional theory (DFT) calculations show that HD binds most favorably in the c-pore region, with a binding energy of approximately −12.5 kcal/mol, and similarly favorable stabilization in confined micropore environments, whereas substantially weaker binding is observed in the mesopore. Molecular dynamics simulations also reveal sharply different pore residence patterns: HD localizes predominantly in micropores, occupying this region for ∼80% of the trajectory, while HDO samples larger pore environments more broadly, with ∼45% mesopore and ∼34% c-pore occupancy. This pore-selective behavior persists under mixed HD/HDO coadsorption conditions, demonstrating that reactant–product differentiation is intrinsic to the NU-1000 pore network rather than an artifact of isolated single-component simulations. Radial distribution functions further show that HD is stabilized by dispersion-dominated confinement and weak halogen–hydrogen contacts, whereas HDO is governed by more localized, orientation-dependent interactions with hydrated zirconium node sites. These interaction differences produce a pronounced transport asymmetry, with HDO exhibiting a self-diffusion coefficient of 10.6 ± 2.11 × 10–10 m2/s compared with 0.5 ± 0.09 × 10–10 m2/s for HD at comparable loading. The results identify NU-1000 as a dual-function molecular host that couples reactant retention with product mobility, providing an interface-level mechanism relevant to selective CWA detoxification and confined transport in hierarchical porous catalysts.

title: A Comprehensive Review and Future Prospects of Aluminum–Sulfur Batteries: From Material Design to Practical Challenges
abstract: ABSTRACT Aluminum–sulfur (Al–S) batteries are promising next‐generation energy storage systems owing to the high abundance, low cost, and multi‐electron redox capability of Al, combined with the high theoretical capacity and environmental friendliness of S. This review systematically compares the dual electrochemical mechanisms based on S reduction (S 0 /S 2− ) and S oxidation (S 0 /S 4+ ), highlighting their distinct advantages in energy density and safety. Key strategies for cathode design—including carbon‐based, anchoring‐functional, and catalytic‐functional hosts—are discussed, alongside electrolyte engineering using ionic liquids, deep eutectic solvents, inorganic molten salts, and aqueous systems. Recent advances in dendrite suppression, anode protective layers, and functional separators are also summarized. A central challenge identified is the sluggish Al 3+ solvation/desolvation kinetics, which limits rate capability and low‐temperature performance. The application of in situ/operando characterization techniques (XANES, Raman, UV–vis) to unravel complex reaction pathways is emphasized. By integrating multidisciplinary innovations, this review provides a comprehensive perspective and a phased commercialization roadmap, aiming to accelerate the transition of Al–S batteries from laboratory research to practical green energy storage.

title: Graphene-Like-Armored Nanosheet Assemblies toward Fast and Stable High-Mass-Loading Sodium Storage
abstract: Abstract Sodium-ion batteries represent promising energy storage devices, yet their deployment is severely hampered by sluggish ion-transport kinetics and unstable electrode–electrolyte interfacial chemistry that deteriorate rate capability and cycling lifespan, particularly under high-loading electrode configurations. Here, we report a structural anode design comprising double-shelled TiO2 spheres assembled from cross-distributed 2 nm thick nanosheets and uniformly encapsulated by a graphene-like armor. This architecture enables predominantly surface-controlled sodium storage behavior with ultrafast reaction kinetics and exceptional stability, overcoming the long-standing trade-off between capacity, rate performance, and cycle life. The rationally designed electrode achieves a practically relevant areal capacity of 2.13 mAh cm–2 and outstanding rate capability (121 mAh g–1 at 100 C). Remarkably, it remains more than 90% of its capacity over 3,000 cycles at 5 C under a high mass loading of 10.5 mg cm–2, outperforming conventional anode structures. This work establishes a structural design strategy for advanced anodes applicable in practical high-power batteries.

title: Designing an Emulsion-Templated Pentablock Copolymer for Hierarchical Porosity
abstract: Abstract Hierarchically porous polymers integrate macro-, meso-, and micropores to enhance mass transport, diffusion, and specific surface area, making them attractive for applications in filtration, separation, and storage. Here, an innovative pentablock copolymer (PBC), synthesized using sequential atom transfer radical polymerizations (ATRPs), was designed so that each block would contribute a distinct level of porosity to a hierarchically porous monolith. First, a triblock copolymer with hyper-cross-linkable polystyrene (PS) end-blocks was synthesized from a macroinitiator based on a degradable polycaprolactone (PCL) diol. The PBC was then synthesized by adding cross-linkable poly(glycidyl methacrylate) (PGMA) end-blocks to the PS-b-PCL-b-PS. The PBC was used to form the external phase of an oil-in-oil medium internal phase emulsion and then cross-linked via the PGMA’s epoxide groups to generate a macroporous monolith. Selectively etching the sacrificial PCL midblocks in the emulsion-templated monolith generated mesopores. Hyper-cross-linking the PS blocks generated micropores and etched some of the PCL, generating mesopores. This multiblock pore-generation strategy enabled control over the hierarchical nature of the porous structure, providing a rational approach to designing robust, tunable porous monoliths for advanced applications.

title: Alkylene Spacer Engineering for Boosting Circularly Polarized Luminescence in Homopolypeptide Self-Assembly
abstract: Abstract Functional materials with circularly polarized luminescence (CPL) property featuring both high luminescence efficiency and strong chiroptical activity are highly desirable for advanced photonic applications such as three-dimensional displays, optical encryption, asymmetric photochemistry, and biomedical imaging, yet remain challenging to develop. While extensive efforts have focused on engineering chromophore structures and chiral building blocks, the influence of the spacer connecting luminophores and chiral scaffolds on CPL generation remains poorly understood. Herein, we report an alkylene spacer engineering strategy to regulate supramolecular chirality and CPL performance in homopolypeptide-based assemblies. A series of luminescent homopolypeptides were synthesized, bearing an achiral terminal luminophore connected to the backbone through alkylene spacers of varying lengths. By self-assembly, nanotoroid-dispersed aqueous solutions were obtained from these homopolypeptides with photoluminescence quantum yields exceeding 50%. Despite their nearly identical morphologies, the assemblies exhibited markedly different CPL activities. Increasing the spacer length led to continuous enhancement of CPL performance, with the luminescence dissymmetry factor (glum) increasing by an order of magnitude from 1.1 × 10–3 to 1.1 × 10–2. Structural characterization and molecular simulations reveal that spacer elongation strengthens the coupling between the terminal luminophore and helical polypeptide scaffold, facilitating more efficient chirality transfer and supramolecular chirality amplification within the toroidal assemblies. Further optimizing the degree of polymerization promotes supramolecular ordering and amplifies CPL activity, yielding an enhanced glum up to 1. 8 × 10–2. This work reveals a previously overlooked role of spacer-mediated chirality communication between the terminal luminophore and helical polypeptide scaffolds and establishes alkylene spacer length as a critical structural parameter for chirality amplification in this supramolecular CPL system, providing new insights into the “molecular structure – supramolecular assembly – chiroptical property” relationship.

title: Supramolecular structuring of nanoparticle ligand shells revealed by liquid-phase AFM
abstract: Abstract Polymer grafts are a ubiquitous component of nanocrystal (NC) ligand shells and impart critical functionalities, including biocompatibility and colloidal stability. Although many techniques have been used for elucidating the supramolecular structure of polymer chains once grafted to the NC surface, few of these are able to provide a complete picture of the ligand shell under experimentally relevant conditions ( e.g ., low polymer densities, various solvent environments). Here, we use high-resolution atomic force microscopy imaging along with coarse-grained molecular dynamics simulations to directly image polymers grafted onto single Ag NCs in both air and water to better understand the ligand-solvent interactions that dictate ligand shell structuring. For hydrophobic grafts under poor solvent conditions, the grafts self-associate to form a patchy shell, as previously reported. However, for hydrophilic grafts under good solvent conditions, this patchy morphology persists and is observed even for polyethylene glycol-functionalized NCs (i.e. PEGylated) in water. Polymer structuring is also observed amongst assembled NCs, with the formation of polymer bridges forming across patches. These unexpected results suggest that surface patchiness may be more widespread in colloidal NC systems than previously assumed, and this surface heterogeneity could play an important role in governing collective NC phenomena such as self-assembly.

title: Template‐free tuning of magnetic nanoparticle self‐assemblies in response to external electric and magnetic fields
abstract: Abstract Nanochains made up from one‐dimensional assemblies of magnetic nanoparticles are highly promising for a wide range of applications. Reliable control over their aspect ratio and spatial distribution on substrates is essential for developing functional materials with tailored properties. This study demonstrates that the responses of electrostatically charged aerosol magnetic nanoparticles to electric and magnetic fields enable template‐free self‐assembly of nanochains with tunable average length and spatial distribution directly onto substrates. These results establish charged aerosol magnetic nanoparticle self‐assembly as a versatile approach for fabricating advanced functional materials through a continuous, scalable direct integration of tunable nanochains into devices and substrates relevant to applications.

title: Sequence Dependence of Folding and Self-Assembly of Glycine-X Repeat Peptides on Graphite
abstract: Abstract Cyclic peptides consisting of glycine-X repeats have been shown in simulation and experiment to fold at the graphite–water interface into beta-hairpins, which then self-assemble by intermolecular hydrogen bonding. In this contribution, we investigate the role of the hairpin turn sequence, strand length, and the X amino acid on folding and self-assembly. Simulations of relatively large systems with 9 initially unfolded peptides allow us to observe spontaneous folding, which, together with free energy profiles as a function of RMSD, enable comparison of folding thermodynamics and kinetics among sequences and identification of metastable misfolded conformations. Likewise, spontaneous assembly also occurs in these simulations, which, together with absolute binding free energy calculations, enable comparison of assembly kinetics and preferences for different intermolecular alignments. We find that the GPGG sequence best enforces folding with the desired hairpin turn compared to GGGG and GDGG sequences. While our previous peptide design was head-to-tail cyclized, here, we demonstrate that disulfide cyclization is a viable alternative. Peptides having strands with GT, GA, GG, GS, and GD repeats, as well as those with charge-complementary GE/GZ pairs (where Z is diaminobutyric acid), can fold correctly, but vary in their folding free energy, tendency to adopt misfolded conformations, folding cooperativity, and preference for different intermolecular alignments. GT-repeat strands most favor folding into the desired beta-strands; however, they yield the weakest intermolecular assembly. GG-repeats yield the strongest intermolecular assembly, but peptides with all GG repeats show a greater tendency to misfold. GA-repeat strands exhibit strong folding cooperativity─folding becomes more favorable in the presence of other folded peptides. A peptide with GE repeats on one strand and GZ on the other yields assemblies with alternating negative and positive strands.

title: Multicomponent optical response from stimuli responsive nanocomposite materials
abstract: Natural photonic materials frequently exhibit ordered architectures spanning several length scales, a feature that gives rise to unique functionalities. Replicating elements of this hierarchical organization in synthetic systems is driven by potential applications in photonic technologies, anti-counterfeiting, and chemical sensing. Cellulose nanocrystals (CNCs) are rod-shaped colloids that can organize into chiral nematic liquid-crystalline arrangements when dispersed above a critical concentration. CNCs can provide a route to photonic architectures by exhibiting visible color through selective reflection. In this study, we develop CNC hydrogel nanocomposite photoresists suitable for direct laser writing (DLW) by 2-photon polymerization. Optimization of evaporation-driven self-assembly was used to establish a chiral nematic organization prior to fabrication. DLW then enabled high-resolution fabrication, while the printed structures demonstrated adjustable optical behaviour in response to both solvent exposure and changes in ambient humidity. These results highlight the promise of CNC-based photopolymer composites as multifunctional photoresists that combine hierarchical structural organization, mechanical reinforcement, and responsive photonic properties.

title: An Atomic-Scale Chemical Switch for Oxide Ferroelectricity
abstract: Abstract Interfacial chemistry offers new opportunities for designing ferroelectric materials, yet their coupling with intrinsic polarization remains largely unexplored. Here, we synthesize ferroelectric BiFeO3 nanoparticles with {100} facets covered by a Bi2FeO6-x Aurivillius-like phase, allowing the interfacial Bi2O2 layer to interact with bulk polarization at different relative orientations. Using atomic-resolution scanning transmission electron microscopy, we observed a large polarization enhancement when the interface aligned with the bulk polarization, and a polarization reversal when opposing it. In situ heating and first-principles calculations show that the Bi2O2 layer repels the underlying FeO6 octahedra, which either rotate or rigidly displace to accommodate the chemical stress, depending on local geometry. Moreover, this mechanism can imprint local polarization in Aurivillius phases and nonferroelectric oxides, offering a general route to design polar topologies in oxide heterostructures.

title: Wavelength-Selective Magneto-Optical Diodes Based on Rare-Earth Chiral Molecular Crystals
abstract: Abstract Chiral materials, integrating structural breaking of mirror-symmetry, exhibit physical properties that cannot be observed in centrosymmetric analogues. Among these properties, optical magneto-chiral anisotropy, the nonreciprocal absorption of light shown by chiral magnetized systems, is emerging as an enabling technology in magneto-optics and photonics. Here, we report on enantiopure chiral molecular crystals based on the erbium(III) rare-earth ion that display nonreciprocal, wavelength-selective, magnetic field-induced variations of the optical absorption coefficients up to ca. 200% for the intrashell f–f electronic transition falling in the 1.5 μm telecom wavelength range. Such a response is associated with an exceptionally high Magneto-Chiral Dichroism induced by the strong spin–orbit coupling of the Er(III) and the helical chirality at the lanthanide center, exalted by the magnetic-dipole-allowed character of the electronic transition. This chirality-induced nonreciprocal magneto-optical response represents a proof of concept for the use of these chiral crystalline molecular materials as potential components in magneto-optical diodes.

title: NMR Spectroscopic Evidence for Magnetically Induced Ring Currents in All-Metal-Aromatic [Bi4]4+
abstract: Abstract Experimental assignment of aromaticity in all-metal systems remains challenging, particularly for heavy-element clusters, where local magnetic effects can obscure signatures of circular electron delocalization. Here, we investigate a supramolecularly stabilized, formally tetracationic [Bi4]4+ ring by combining structurally meaningful reference compounds, solid- and solution-state NMR spectroscopy, SQUID magnetometry, and exact two-component relativistic calculations. Comparison with an isostructural [Li4Br]3+-encapsulated analogue and a binuclear Bi(III) reference compound disentangles global ring-current effects from local heavy-atom deshielding and ligand-specific conformational effects. On this basis, the unusually downfield-shifted 1H and 13C NMR signals observed for the Bi4-containing species provide direct spectroscopic evidence for magnetically induced ring currents in the [Bi4]4+ core. By contrast, bulk magnetic measurements do not reveal significant diamagnetic exaltation, indicating that this quantity is not a resolved descriptor of aromaticity in these systems. Stoichiometric studies further identify chemically competent intermediates that provide mechanistic snapshots of [Bi4]4+ ring formation. Complementary calculations support the assignment of a magnetically responsive, σ-delocalized [Bi4]4+ core, reproduce a rare spectroscopically observed puckering motion of the rhomboidal [Bi4]4+, and underscore the critical role of spin–orbit coupling on electronic structure and dynamics. Overall, this work moves the discussion of aromaticity from predominantly computational assignment toward experimentally benchmarked analysis in the heavy-element and all-metal regime.

title: Double-network silica–polyacrylamide composite aerogels with enhanced mechanical integrity and multifunctional adsorption performance
abstract: Abstract A facile strategy was developed to synthesize silica/polyacrylamide composite aerogels that simultaneously exhibit high mechanical strength and large surface area. An interpenetrated organic polyacrylamide network was incorporated within the silica framework without additional cross-linkers, enabling efficient stress distribution and enhanced structural integrity. The optimized TDB-Pam(2 M) composite aerogel possesses a homogeneous mesoporous network with a specific surface area of 774 m 2 g -1 , low density (0.346 g cm -3 ), and superior compressive strength (22.3 MPa) with a Young’s modulus of 25.3 MPa. The incorporation of amide-rich polyacrylamide also provided selective binding sites for heavy-metal ions, achieving more than 90% Hg 2+ removal efficiency and a Langmuir maximum adsorption capacity of 626.79 mg g -1 for TDB-Pam(2 M). This synthesis route provides an effective approach to fabricate mechanically reinforced, multifunctional silica-based aerogels applicable to environmental purification and other advanced porous-material applications.

title: Birch-Type-Reduced Carbazole Anions Enable Redox-Adaptive Super-Reducing Photocatalysis
abstract: Abstract Photocatalytic activation of inert chemical bonds is constrained by the redox potential of the catalyst. Here, we report a redox-adaptive photocatalytic strategy in which an electron-rich carbazole photocatalyst, CBZ6, functions as a molecular redox transformer through the formation of Birch-type carbazole anions. Under visible light, CBZ6 switches between a neutral state for conventional photoredox reactions and an anionic state for super-reducing catalysis. Excitation of the anionic state generates a super-reducing species with an excited-state oxidation potential of approximately −3.6 V versus SCE, substantially beyond that of the neutral excited state (−2.2 V). This adaptive redox switching enables activation of otherwise inaccessible C–F bonds in aryl fluorides, polyfluoroalkyl compounds, and fluoropolymers. The complementary reactivities of the two states further enable diverse photoredox transformations, establishing redox adaptation as a strategy for expanding the accessible reactivity of organic photocatalysts.

title: Deciphering Interheme Electron-Transfer Pathways in a Diheme Peroxidase from Methane-Oxidizing Bacteria
abstract: Abstract Bis-FeIV-forming enzymes represent an emerging paradigm in high-valent heme iron chemistry, in which two hemes separated by 15–20 Å are both oxidized to the FeIV state. A tryptophan positioned between the two hemes in two out of the three known enzymes to form this state, MauG and MbnH, has been proposed as the dominant pathway for interheme electron transfer. .The third enzyme, BthA, instead has a serine at this position. Here, we used site-directed mutagenesis of Trp113 in MbnH to test whether this tryptophan is uniquely required for interheme electron transfer. Computational pathway analysis identified the possibility of an alternative, noncovalent route mediated by Arg283 and a heme propionate with possible electronic coupling comparable to that of the native tryptophan pathway. Consistent with this prediction, only simultaneous disruption of both the tryptophan and propionate-mediated pathways abolished bis-FeIV formation entirely. Moreover, only mutants capable of forming bis-FeIV retained the ability to turnover substrate, directly establishing this high-valent state as the catalytic intermediate responsible for substrate modification. These results demonstrate that an intervening tryptophan is not required for fast interheme electron transfer, and instead reveal an additional, noncovalent pathway that may be a general feature of diheme peroxidases.

title: Engineering a Reconfigurable Transmembrane Receptor Enables Logic-Controlled Signal Translocation
abstract: Abstract Transmembrane receptors relay extracellular cues into intracellular responses through reconfigurable conformational changes, yet engineering synthetic systems that emulate receptor-like signal translocation with programmable control remains challenging. Here, we engineer a reconfigurable transmembrane receptor that enables logic-controlled signal translocation across lipid membranes. The receptor is constructed from an oriented Y-shaped triplex DNA architecture that inserts directionally into the plasma membrane via dual cholesterol anchors and integrates two environmental inputs─H+ and ATP─through an i-motif and an aptamer module. Under dual-input conditions, cooperative duplex-to-triplex switching triggers reconfigurable structural rearrangement and drives transmembrane relocation of a signaling strand from the outer to the inner membrane leaflet. This receptor-mediated signal translocation converts extracellular chemical cues into spatially defined intracellular activation. The repositioned strand serves as a modular intracellular effector that can be functionalized to implement programmable reactions, including bioorthogonal catalysis and light-triggered photocatalysis at the membrane interface. Importantly, endogenous tumor-microenvironmental cues trigger receptor reconfiguration and signal translocation in 3D tumor spheroids and in vivo, enabling logic-gated intracellular photocatalysis and &gt;85% tumor growth inhibition in xenograft models. By coupling logic-gated reconfigurable switching with directional transmembrane signal propagation, this work establishes an engineered transmembrane receptor for programmable intracellular activation and provides a general strategy for synthetic signal translocation in living systems.

title: Circular RNA Delivery In Vitro and In Vivo Using Doubly Branched Aminoethoxy-Functionalized Ionizable Lipid Nanoparticles
abstract: Abstract Circular RNA is a therapeutically promising RNA modality with superior stability and extended protein expression relative to linear RNA. While delivery systems for linear RNA have received much attention, less effort has been directed toward the delivery of circular RNA, whose closed topology and physicochemical properties differ from those of linear RNAs. Here, we disclose a class of ionizable lipids that enable efficient in vitro and in vivo delivery of circular RNA. These ionizable lipids are step-economically accessible, allowing facile assessment of their structure–delivery relationships. Our studies reveal key elements that enhance circular RNA delivery in vitro and in vivo, including aminoethoxy head units, doubly branched tails and linkers tuned for hydrogen bonding and biodegradability. The lead ionizable lipid for circular RNA delivery, iL-19, incorporating these features, achieves ∼28-fold higher protein expression in C2C12 myocytes than Moderna’s SM-102 formulation and 2.5-fold higher expression upon intramuscular administration in BALB/c mice. iL-19 also surpasses benchmark ionizable lipids ALC-0315 (7.8-fold) and DLin-MC3-DMA (33.4-fold) for intramuscular circular RNA delivery in vivo under otherwise identical conditions. This study establishes design principles and a step-economical synthesis for accessing ionizable lipids that enable highly efficient in vitro and in vivo circular RNA delivery.

title: Selective Consecutive Decarboxylation Enables Skeletal Contraction of Waste PET
abstract: Abstract Direct catalytic upcycling of waste polyethylene terephthalate (PET) to benzene through consecutive decarboxylation contracts the terephthalate-derived C8 framework to C6, representing a skeletal-editing strategy for aromatic polycarboxylates. The key challenge is to control pathway selection across consecutive decarboxylation steps, favoring sequential aryl–carboxyl C–C bond cleavage over competing hydrogenolysis while preserving the aromatic core. Herein, we report an efficient direct catalytic conversion of waste PET to benzene, achieving an exceptionally high yield of 83.3% over a tailored Ru/W0.4ZrOx catalyst. The performance arises from synergistic acid-site reconstruction and oxygen-vacancy engineering. Moderate WOx incorporation into ZrO2 converts Lewis acidity into Brønsted acidity, while oxygen vacancies and WOx species promote adsorption and activation of carboxyl groups. In cooperation with Ru nanoparticles, these features preferentially stabilize the decarboxylation intermediate over its hydrogenolysis counterpart, directing both consecutive steps toward C–C bond cleavage while suppressing undesired hydrogenolysis pathways. Controlled hydrogen supply and a deliberately designed dodecane/water mixed solvent system further enhance selectivity. The catalyst performs effectively across diverse real-world PET wastes, with preliminary techno-economic and life-cycle analyses indicating favorable process-level metrics under the evaluated assumptions. More broadly, these mechanistic insights establish synergistic acidity and oxygen-vacancy regulation as a catalyst-design principle for decarboxylative skeletal editing of aromatic polycarboxylates.

title: Electroanalytical and Computational Investigation of Oxoammonium-Mediated Hydride Transfer
abstract: Abstract Oxoammonium-mediated hydride transfer is an important yet relatively underexplored elementary step in C–H functionalization. In this work, we employed cyclic voltammetry (CV) to measure the rates of hydride transfer between electrochemically generated oxoammonium catalysts and 42 substrates including ethers, carbamates, amides, and sulfonamides. Through quantum mechanical (QM) calculations, we uncovered a new transition-state model for hydride transfer in which the N atom of the catalyst resides near a heteroatom (X = N or O) of the substrate to allow alignment of the oxoammonium’s O═N+ motif and the substrate’s forming C═X+ bond. Energy decomposition analysis was subsequently performed to elucidate the key factors that govern the kinetics of oxoammonium-mediated hydride transfer. Beyond conventional electronic and steric considerations, we identified substrate distortion, secondary orbital interactions, and noncovalent interactions as critical factors that influence hydride transfer reactivity. We anticipate that these kinetic data along with the mechanistic insights they provide will inform future catalyst development and synthetic applications to broaden the scope of oxoammonium catalysis.

title: Metal Fluorides: All-In-One Supports for Ruthenium-Catalyzed Ammonia Synthesis
abstract: Abstract Ammonia, an emerging energy carrier, demands advanced catalysts for synthesis under mild conditions to integrate with green hydrogen. We herein establish a family of metal fluoride supports (MFn, M = Li, Na, K, Mg, Ca, or Ba) as a tunable “all-in-one” platform for ruthenium (Ru) catalysts. These Ru/MFn systems unify the critical merits of various existing catalysts, such as support-mediated activation of reactants and air stability. Varying the host cation can direct the catalytic pathway. Consequently, Ru/NaF exhibits excellent turnover frequency, while Ru/BaF2 delivers an NH3 synthesis rate of 58.0 mmolNH3 gcat–1 h–1 at 400 °C and 0.9 MPa─surpassing all reported Ru-based catalysts with ≤4 wt % Ru and without external promoters. Advanced characterization reveals that the fluorine vacancy formation energies of the alkali and alkaline-earth lattices, together with the vacancy-reactant interactions, dictate the divergent catalytic mechanisms mediated by different active sites. This work expands the chemistry of metal fluorides, launching a new paradigm for potentially viable NH3-synthesis under mild conditions.

title: Cesium-Induced Stabilization of the FeOOH Cocatalyst on Bismuth Vanadate Photoanode for Ultraefficient and Stable Photoelectrochemical Water Oxidation
abstract: Abstract Developing active and durable water oxidation cocatalysts is essential for advancing photoelectrochemical (PEC) water-splitting systems. This study investigates the cesium-induced reconstruction of the FeOOH cocatalyst on a bismuth vanadate (BVO) photoanode for the water oxidation reaction, with a focus on the reconstruction process and its effect in improving interfacial charge transfer and photostability. Cesium ions induce the reconstruction of Fe species on the BVO/FeOOH photoanode during the PEC process, leading to the formation of a robust Cs-incorporated FeOOH (Cs:FeOOH) catalytic layer. Spectroscopic analysis combined with open-circuit potential measurement reveals that the in situ formed Cs:FeOOH cocatalyst can effectively protect BVO and promote interfacial hole transfer during PEC operation. As a result, the BVO/Cs:FeOOH photoanode achieves a photocurrent density of 6.29 mA cm–2 at 1.23 V vs. RHE and maintains stable operation for over 100 h. Furthermore, the Cs-incorporated FeOOH cocatalyst strategy can be extended to other semiconductor systems, including TiO2 and FeOx, highlighting its broader potential for improving solar-driven PEC water oxidation.

title: Regio- and Enantioselective Functionalization of Gaseous Alkanes via Nickel-Catalyzed Alkene Dicarbofunctionalization
abstract: Abstract The regio- and enantioselective functionalization of gaseous alkanes remains an unsolved challenge in organic synthesis. Here, we report a general strategy for the asymmetric three-component dicarbofunctionalization of alkenes using readily available gaseous alkanes, including ethane, propane, and isobutane. This transformation, enabled by the merger of hydrogen atom transfer photocatalysis with a chiral nickel catalyst, efficiently delivers chiral α-aryl carbonyl compounds in good yield with excellent regio- and enantioselectivity (up to &gt;20:1 rr and 99:1 er). Experimental and computational studies reveal insights into the mechanism controlling selectivity. Operating under exceptionally mild, energy-efficient conditions, the method unlocks a versatile platform for upgrading feedstock gaseous alkanes into sought-after chiral building blocks.

title: Hydrogenation of CO2 to Propane and n -Butane by Engineering Metal Oxide Interfacial Structure and Manipulating Zeolite Pore Structure and Acidity
abstract: Abstract Selective hydrogenation of CO2 to propane and n-butane is of great interest, as these two compounds are not only primary components of liquefied petroleum gas (LPG) but also crucial raw materials for preparing propene and a degradable plastic precursor of succinic acid. Although various composite catalysts combining metal oxides and zeolites have been explored, their catalytic performances remain insufficient. Here, we found that ZnZrOx decorated with ultrasmall FeOx clusters, forming an intimate FeOx–ZnZrOx interfacial structure, showed high catalytic activity for CO2 hydrogenation to methanol due to a strong CO2 adsorption capacity and H2 dissociation ability, and silicoaluminophosphate molecular sieve with RHO topological structure enhanced methanol conversion into propane and n-butane via hexamethylbenzenes as active hydrocarbon pool species owing to its unique supercage structure and double eight-membered ring pore opening. As a result, coupling of these two materials delivers a CO2 conversion of ∼66% and a (propane + n-butane) selectivity of 82% in hydrocarbons, which leads to a (propane + n-butane) yield of ∼42%. It is surprising that this composite preferentially produces n-butane rather than iso-butane, and the n-butane/iso-butane ratio is higher than 85.8. The high catalytic stability of this composite is demonstrated by maintaining CO2 conversion, (propane + n-butane) selectivity in hydrocarbons, and their yield of ∼ 61%, ∼ 77%, and ∼ 31%, respectively, after a reaction of 620 h. This work not only fabricates a high-performance catalyst for CO2 hydrogenation to propane and n-butane by engineering the metal oxide interfacial structure and manipulating the zeolite’s pore structure and acidity, but also makes it possible to develop an efficient way for preparing propene and succinic acid from CO2 hydrogenation.

title: Biomaterial‐Based Controlled Release Systems for Spinal Cord Remyelination
abstract: ABSTRACT Spinal cord injury (SCI) triggers a complex secondary injury cascade characterized by oligodendrocyte (OL) death and axonal demyelination, leading to permanent neurological deficits. Despite the presence of endogenous oligodendrocyte progenitor cells (OPCs), the inhibitory microenvironment—marked by inflammation, glial scarring, and biochemical barriers—prevents effective remyelination. Traditional pharmacological treatments are further hindered by the blood‐spinal cord barrier and rapid clearance of intrathecal injections. This review examines the evolution of controlled release systems engineered to modulate the oligodendroglial lineage. We analyze macro‐ and micro‐scale platforms, including scaffolds, which provide mechanical and topographical cues to direct the fate of OLs and OPCs. Furthermore, we discuss advanced nanoscale vectors, such as nanoparticles and exosomes, designed to deliver high‐value payloads—including small molecules and therapeutic oligonucleotides—directly to the lesion site while minimizing systemic toxicity. Finally, we address critical translational gaps to bridge the divide between preclinical innovation and clinical application in restoring neural connectivity.

title: Silicate Biomaterials‐Stimulated Vascularized Callus Organoids for Bone Tissue Regeneration
abstract: ABSTRACT Organoids that recapitulate native fracture callus can form spontaneous ossification centers within a bone defect, offering substantial promise for rapid bone regeneration. However, existing callus organoids generally lack a functional vascular network and an appropriate mechanical microenvironment, and their production limits scalability and uniformity. Here, we established a droplet‐based microfluidic platform for the high‐throughput generation of morphology‐dependent magnesium silicate‐engineered composite hydrogel microspheres, enabling the uniform construction of vascularized callus organoids. Importantly, morphology‐dependent magnesium silicate could regulate both the bulk mechanical performance and internal stress distribution of the composite hydrogels. In vitro, callus organoids modulated by magnesium silicate nanotubes significantly promoted chondrogenic and osteogenic differentiation, developed a stable endothelial network and mineralized structure. Furthermore, magnesium silicate nanotube‐engineered composite hydrogel (2NT‐GM) offered a favorable mechanical microenvironment for callus organoids, thereby activating the mechanotransduction‐related pathway for promoting the development of organoids. In a rat femoral condyle critical‐sized defect model, the vascularized callus organoids regulated by 2NT‐GM were further found to significantly promote vascular network formation, and facilitate bone regeneration at the bone defect center within 6 weeks of implantation. Together, this study suggests a promising strategy for bone tissue regeneration by developing vascularized callus organoids with the stimulation of inorganic silicate biomaterials.

title: Remote‐Controlled Genetic Circuits: Light, Ultrasound, and Magnetic Fields for Programmable Gene Regulation
abstract: ABSTRACT Remote‐controlled genetic circuits use externally applied physical signals to regulate gene expression and cellular functions with spatial and temporal precision. Light, ultrasound, and magnetic fields provide complementary advantages in controllability, tissue accessibility, and biological compatibility, but their performance depends on both physical‐field propagation and efficient conversion of external energy into intracellular signals and predictable gene‐regulatory outputs. This review presents a unified framework of physical transduction, biological sensors, signal processors, and genetic effectors for comparing prokaryotic and eukaryotic systems. Core genetic circuits are distinguished from delivery and auxiliary platforms that support cargo release, cellular uptake, or energy conversion without directly regulating genes. Representative systems are compared by circuit architecture, transduction mechanism, stimulus parameters, dynamic range, basal leakage, response kinetics, reversibility, in vivo actuation, delivery requirements, and safety. The evolution from inducible switches toward multi‐input logic, tunable regulation, genetic memory, and feedback control is discussed. An end‐to‐end codesign workflow and modality‐specific reporting framework are proposed to integrate physical inputs, transducers, genetic circuits, delivery strategies, and stimulation devices. Quantitative benchmarking and standardized safety evaluation are essential for advancing these systems toward predictable and clinically translatable therapeutic platforms.

title: Vacancy‐Associated La–Ir Pairs Enable Water‐Derived Oxygen‐Hydroxyl Coupling for Durable Low‐Ir PEM Water Electrolysis
abstract: ABSTRACT Developing highly stable, low‐iridium catalysts is critical for acidic oxygen evolution, but is limited by structural degradation driven by acid corrosion and voltage polarization. Herein, we report an iridium and lanthanum co‐doped manganese‐cobalt spinel catalyst, Ir,La‐MCO δ , featuring octahedral La–Ir pairs (La oct –Ir oct ) with a theoretical favorable configuration of adjacent bridging and Ir z ‐axis oxygen vacancies. This low‐Ir catalyst Ir,La‐MCO δ (0.12 mg Ir cm −2 ) exhibits an overpotential of merely 220 mV at 10 mA cm −2 in pH = 1 electrolyte, and demonstrates robust operation for over 1550 h at 1 A cm −2 in a proton exchange membrane (PEM) water electrolyzer. Coupled (quasi)in situ characterizations and operando spectroscopy reveal that the adjacent oxygen vacancies mediate the evolution of oxygen intermediates, enabling water‐derived oxygen‐hydroxyl coupling with negligible lattice oxygen involvement, via a decoupled proton–electron transfer pathway. This mechanism preserves the structural integrity of the catalyst and yields a calculated reaction free‐energy change of merely 0.38 eV ( U = 1.23 V) for the most unfavorable oxygen‐hydroxyl coupling elementary step, thereby endowing Ir,La‐MCO δ with exceptional durability. This work provides a valuable mechanistic insight into designing highly stable defective catalysts.

title: Artificial Regulatory T Cells Orchestrate Phase‐Spanning Regeneration in Refractory Tissue Injuries
abstract: ABSTRACT Regulatory T cells (Tregs) possess potent multiphasic reparative capacity; however, their application is limited by ethical and regulatory challenges associated with live cell therapies. Treg‐derived exosomes (TExo) exhibit low immunogenicity while enriching regenerative signaling relative to parental Tregs. Current exosome carriers place greater emphasis on sustained release than on factors affecting vesicle stability, such as nonspecific interactions and confinement effects. Inspired by the multivesicular body (MVB), we engineered artificial Tregs (ATregs) with an MVB‐like architecture that integrates vesicle protection with sustained release through a reconstructed storage microenvironment. This design enables phase‐aligned TExo release and extends functional activity by more than an order of magnitude compared with free TExo. ATregs sequentially coordinate the suppression of inflammation, enhancement of angiogenesis, and stimulation of skin appendage regeneration. In diabetic wounds and deep second‐degree burn models, which represent intrinsic repair dysfunction and severe structural tissue loss, ATregs markedly accelerate healing and outperform conventional strategies across murine and porcine models. These findings overcome the key limitations of exosome therapies and open a new avenue for next‐generation regenerative therapeutics.

title: Myelin Sheath-Inspired Fluorocarbon Hydrophobic Bridges for Stable n-Type Organic Mixed Ionic–Electronic Conductors
abstract: Abstract Operationally stable n-type organic mixed ionic–electronic conductors (OMIECs) remain a critical bottleneck for organic electrochemical transistors (OECTs) for application in bioelectronic and neuromorphic devices. However, several state-of-the-art n-type OMIECs suffer from performance decay and poor stability when operated in aqueous media. Inspired by myelin sheaths, we challenge the conventional “π-backbone + hydrophilic side-chain” design and propose a molecular architecture with fluorocarbon hydrophobic bridges to spatially segregate, at the molecular level, ionic and electronic pathways. By tuning the fluorocarbon bridge chain length in fluorocarbon-ethylene glycol chain substituents [−CH2(CF2)nCH2(OCH2CH2)5OMe = 2nFG; n = 1, 2, 3, 4, 6] of a DPP-CNTVT polymer series (2nFG-P), we balance electron transport, ion exchange, redox chemistry efficiency, and water incorporation. Extensive in situ spectroelectrochemistry, EIS, Raman, EQCM-D, AFM, and GIWAXS characterization reveals that tuning the length of the hydrophobic bridge enables good electron transport, suppresses excessive water incorporation, and enhances stability. Thus, the polymer with a mid-length bridge, 8FG-P (n = 4), achieves the greatest electron transport (μC* ∼ 157 F cm–1 V–1 s–1, μ ∼ 1.22 cm2 V–1 s–1), fastest response (τon/τoff = 2.6/1.5 ms), and retains &gt;90% of the initial performance after 10,000 s of operation in water, a result independent of the polymer molecular weight. This strategy potentially expands OMIECs design principles and offers useful insights toward stable n-type OECT semiconductors.

title: Sustainable Development of Interconnected Hierarchical Porous Carbon From Rice Panicle Waste: Synergistic KOH / CO 2 Dual‐Activation Strategy for Advanced Symmetric Supercapacitors
abstract: ABSTRACT Herein, agricultural waste of rice panicles was adopted as a raw precursor to prepare PAC using KOH activation at different concentrations (0, 0.25, 0.50, and 0.75 M) coupled with CO 2 activation at 850°C and its implementation as symmetric supercapacitor electrodes. RPPAC‐0.25‐850 exhibited high S BET , hierarchical porosity, and a high degree of graphitization. At 1 A g −1 , RPPAC‐0.25‐850 attained a gravimetric capacitance of 280 F g −1 , Coulombic efficiency of 86.53%, and an impressive energy density of 38.95 Wh kg −1 at a power density of 413.5 W kg −1 . Likewise, the RPPAC‐0.25‐850‐based symmetric SC device exhibited high GCD cycling stability, retaining 88% capacitance at 10 A g −1 after 6000 GCD cycles, suggesting superior capacitance efficiency. The results suggest that agricultural waste can be a sustainable energy storage solution, with optimal KOH activation conditions for exceptional SC performance, and also offers a viable potential route for greener, more efficient energy solutions.
